Tuner Drops New Body Kit for the Old F80 BMW M3
11 photos
Photo: Instagram | revozportt
Just because you own an older generation of the BMW M3 does not mean that you cannot make it more special, because there are numerous aftermarket upgrades available for it, and some of them have been signed by renowned tuners.
In this case, we are talking about RevoZport, which recently took to its social media channels to release these pictures, which depict a modded F80 M3. Mind you, that’s the older model, which was made from 2014 to 2018, and was offered strictly as a four-door sedan, with pure rear-wheel drive, and a 3-liter twin-turbo straight-six paired either with a six-speed manual or a seven-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission.
Speaking of the mill, you should know that it produced 425 hp (317 kW /431 ps) and 406 lb-ft (550 Nm) of torque. That’s not bad at all, even by today’s standards, and the same can be said about the performance numbers, too. With 4.1 seconds needed to hit 62 mph (100 kph) from a standstill, this generation of the BMW M3 was pretty much as fast as today’s base M3. The top speed was electronically limited to 155 mph (250 kph).
Photo: Instagram | revozportt Now, the pictured F80 BMW M3 is not about more oomph, but enhanced looks. We can see that the hood is new, and so is the splitter, as well as the add-ons surrounding the side vents in the front bumper. There is new trim on the front fenders, too, and new side skirt attachments are also on deck. The changes continue at the rear, where this car has a massive wing attached to the trunk lid, as well as a new skirt.
The BMW roundels and the M logos are still visible, and that’s a nice touch if you ask me, and in this case, the German sports sedan features a blue look, numerous black details, and tinted windows. The Y-spoke wheels have come from the aftermarket world, and they are bigger than the OEM ones. Moreover, the car also sits closer to the ground, so the suspension has also been modified during the tuning job.
We do not know how much RevoZport’s Aero Body Kit for the F80 BMW M3 costs, as the pricing details haven’t been released at the time of writing. However, interested parties can easily find out everything about the body kit by reaching out to the tuner.
On an unrelated note, the current BMW M3, namely the G80 Sedan (and G81 Touring) will be put to sleep, as a new generation is in the making as we speak. The upcoming M3 will enter the Neue Klasse era. It is expected to feature a mild-hybrid 3-liter twin-turbo powertrain, perhaps with over 600 hp, and word on the street is that it might debut in 2028.
